placements.role: Provides transformers, switchgear, UPS and modular power systems for high-density data centers.

role_evidence.claim: Eaton's 2025 annual report describes medium-voltage transformers, switchgear and the 9395XR UPS for data-center customers.

placements.role: Adds liquid-cooling technology to its data-center infrastructure portfolio through Boyd Thermal.

role_evidence.claim: Eaton's 2025 annual report says its planned Boyd Thermal acquisition adds critical liquid-cooling technology for hyperscale and colocation customers.

business_summary: Eaton Corporation plc is an Ireland-domiciled, NYSE-listed power management company that sells electrical equipment and aerospace systems. Its Electrical sector supplies medium-voltage transformers, switchgear, busway, uninterruptible power supplies and modular power assemblies to utilities, industrials and data centre operators; its Aerospace segment supplies fluid and electrical systems to aircraft programmes. The mapped exposure runs through the electrical side. Eaton announced in the second quarter of 2026 an agreement to separate its Mobility business through a Reverse Morris Trust transaction, which narrows the company further towards electrical.

exposure_summary.narrative: Eaton sits on two links of the ai-infrastructure chain. On power-equipment, the chain's money corner and its most UNDISCOVERED link, it is a direct supplier of the transformers, switchgear, UPS and modular power systems that a high-density campus consumes. On liquid-cooling it is a later entrant: the mapped role evidence rests on the planned Boyd Thermal acquisition rather than on installed product revenue, so the second placement is real but younger than the first. The company's own second-quarter 2026 release names data centres as a key growth driver while explicitly declining to attribute the quarter to them alone.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: Data-centre revenue is not disclosed as a percentage: Eaton's second-quarter 2026 earnings release (accession 0001551182-26-000027) reports Electrical Americas and Electrical Global as segments and names data centres as a growth driver, but publishes no data-centre revenue line or share.

ev_to_sales.basis: Enterprise value 163779362000.0 divided by fiscal year 2025-12-31 revenue 27448000000; share count 387900000 as of 2025-12-31 is the official SEC companyfacts figure; the close 402.78 of 2026-08-28 is the repo's own market plane (data/market/ETN.json, price_status AGREED), not an issuer document.

implied_fcf_cagr.basis: Free-cash-flow CAGR the current enterprise value 163779362000.0 implies over a 5-year explicit period on base FCF 3553000000.0, solved by bisection on FCF CAGR at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. The discount rate and terminal growth are assumed, so the solve is an assumption-dependent expectation reading, not a reported figure.

horizon_spread.basis: Spread between the implied CAGR solved over the shortest and longest explicit periods in quality.reverse_dcf.implied_by_horizon ({'5': 0.2958, '7': 0.2205, '10': 0.1671}). It measures how much of the expectation reading is a horizon convention rather than a statement about price, and inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

crowdedness_caveats: The power-equipment link is scored UNDISCOVERED with a crowdedness score of 38, but Eaton itself is the least un-crowded way to own it: data/market/ETN.json pcs records 25 analysts covering the name and 88.1% institutional ownership as of 2026-08-29, an axis-B band of SATURATED.

Retail attention is the part that is genuinely quiet. The same pcs block reads axis-A DARK with a score of 100.0, and the gate state is ADVISORY because the positive-control fixtures were unreadable in the Actions venue, so the axis-A reading is not machine-certified.

The link's own crowdedness rationale says the corner is institutionally recognised and rarely narrated as an AI trade. That is a statement about narrative, not about ownership, and Eaton's ownership is crowded.

confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. INFERRED is a figure computed from SEC companyfacts, with the derivation named in its basis; where a market price enters the computation the basis says so explicitly, because the price leg is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/ETN.json, price_status AGREED) and not an issuer document. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.
